title: U.S. House · Iowa's 3rd District
area: South-central Iowa, including Des Moines and its suburbs

context.text: Incumbent Zach Nunn (R) advanced unopposed from the June 2, 2026 Republican primary. Sarah Trone Garriott (D), a member of the Iowa State Senate, defeated Jennifer Konfrst, Tracy Limon, and Easton Wolfe in the June 2, 2026 Democratic primary. Cook Political Report rated the district R+2.

summary.text: Nunn is the Republican incumbent, first elected to Iowa's 3rd District in 2022 after four years in the Iowa House and four in the Iowa Senate. A colonel in the Air Force Reserve, he previously worked on cybersecurity policy at the White House National Security Council. He serves on the House Financial Services and Agriculture committees.

background.text: Nunn is a sixth-generation Iowan who, according to his official biography, was raised on Des Moines' east side in a family of public school teachers, nurses, and farmers and attended Southeast Polk High School. Wikipedia gives his birth date as May 4, 1979.

He earned a bachelor's degree in political science and international relations from Drake University (2002), a master's degree in military operational art and science from the U.S. Air Force Air Command and Staff College, and a master's degree from Cambridge University (2007).

Nunn served almost two decades in the U.S. Air Force as an airborne intelligence officer, according to his official biography, deploying three times to the Middle East after 9/11. He is a colonel in the Air Force Reserve.

His civilian career includes working as an adjunct professor of cybersecurity and national policy at Drake University, director of business development at SimSpace Corporation, chief operations officer and national counterintelligence officer with the Office of the Director of National Intelligence, and director of cybersecurity policy and engagement on the White House National Security Council.
Nunn served in the Iowa House of Representatives from 2015 to 2019 and the Iowa Senate from 2019 to 2023.
He won the 3rd District seat in November 2022, defeating incumbent Democrat Cindy Axne 50.3% to 49.6%, and was re-elected in 2024 with about 52% of the vote.

In the 119th Congress he serves on the House Financial Services Committee (including as vice chairman of its national security and illicit finance subcommittee), the House Agriculture Committee, and the House Select Committee on the Chinese Communist Party.
According to his official biography, he lives in Ankeny with his wife Kelly; they have six children, two of them adopted.

priorities.text: Improving the economy, supporting Iowa agriculture, holding government accountable, keeping the country safe, and helping families and kids, according to his official House issues page.
Says tax relief on tips and overtime income and expanded small-business deductions are helping Iowa workers keep more of their pay and giving manufacturers certainty to invest and hire.
Government accountability, including leading the bipartisan Stop Insider Trading Act to ban members of Congress and their immediate families from trading individual stocks while in office.
priorities.quote: Banning stock trades in Congress is about accountability, and every American should demand it from their elected officials.

positions.summary: Highlighted a 2025 spending bill's $150 billion in new border and immigration funding, citing more border patrol agents, expanded detention capacity, and additional surveillance technology as wins he helped secure.
positions.quote: Today, we passed $150 billion in new funding to deliver serious backup for our law enforcement, border agents, and military.

positions.summary: Says he championed the Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act to replenish Israel's Iron Dome missile defense system and provide additional military assistance.
positions.quote: Championing the Israel Security Supplemental Appropriations Act to replenish the Iron Dome and assist our strongest ally in the Middle East as they fight Hamas and other militant groups.

record.text: Served on the House Committee on Agriculture (Commodity Markets, Digital Assets, and Rural Development; General Farm Commodities, Risk Management, and Credit subcommittees) and the Committee on Financial Services (Capital Markets; National Security, Illicit Finance, and International Financial Institutions subcommittees), 2023-2024.
Led the Stop Insider Trading Act, which the House passed 232-198, to prohibit members of Congress and their immediate family members from buying individual stocks while serving in office.

candidates.name: Sarah Trone Garriott
candidates.currentRole: Member, Iowa State Senate, District 14 (since 2023); previously District 22 (2021-2023)

summary.text: Trone Garriott is a Democratic member of the Iowa Senate, an ordained Lutheran minister, and a nonprofit coordinator who was first elected to the legislature in 2020. She has held a Senate seat in the Des Moines suburbs since 2021 and previously served as Senate minority whip. According to her campaign website, she is running to give Iowans a voice in Washington, with an emphasis on health care and working families.

background.text: Born in Minneapolis, Minnesota, she graduated from Cloquet High School and earned a B.A. in history from the College of St. Scholastica (1999).

According to her campaign website, she served a year as an AmeriCorps VISTA volunteer supporting victims of domestic violence and then attended Harvard Divinity School, where she earned an M.A. in theological studies (2003) while working at a women's shelter and a youth nonprofit.

She worked as a hospital chaplain, including at Lurie Children's Hospital in Chicago (2005-2008), and received an M.Div. from the Lutheran School of Theology at Chicago (2008). She is ordained in the Evangelical Lutheran Church in America.
She served as pastor of Martin Luther Evangelical Lutheran Church in Bergton, Virginia, and moved to Iowa in 2013 to lead Faith Lutheran Church in Clive as associate pastor.
She has been coordinator of interfaith engagement for the Des Moines Area Religious Council Food Pantry Network since 2017 and co-founded the Iowa Interfaith Exchange.
She was elected to the Iowa Senate in November 2020 for District 22, winning an open seat held by a retiring Republican with 51.1% of the vote, and took office in January 2021.
After redistricting, she ran in District 14 in 2022 and defeated Senate President Jake Chapman 51.5% to 48.5%; she won re-election in 2024 by 29 votes after a recount.
She served as Senate minority whip during the 90th General Assembly and, in the current session, serves on the Education Committee and as ranking member of the Health and Human Services Committee.
She announced her congressional candidacy on May 5, 2025, and was unopposed in the Democratic primary. According to Wikipedia, she lives in West Des Moines with her husband and two sons.

priorities.text: A higher standard for Washington, growing the economy by investing in people rather than special interests, and making life more affordable.
Affordable health care, protecting public schools, and protecting Iowa's land, water, and clean energy future.

positions.summary: Trone Garriott's campaign issues page lists "Reproductive freedom is personal—and non-negotiable" as one of her core issues.
Trone Garriott's campaign issues page lists "Protecting Iowa's land, water, and clean energy future" as a priority.
Voted no on HF 756 (removing the permit requirement to carry a handgun), which passed the Iowa Senate 31-17 on 2021-03-22.
Voted no on HF 2317 (replacing Iowa's graduated income tax with a 3.9% flat tax), which passed the Iowa Senate 32-16 on 2022-02-24.

record.text: Serves on the Iowa Senate Education, Commerce, Health and Human Services, Natural Resources & Environment, and Health Policy Oversight committees (2025-2026).
Voted no on HF 756 (removing the permit requirement to carry a handgun in Iowa), which passed the Iowa Senate 31-17 on 2021-03-22.
Voted no on SF 413 (an elections bill shortening the absentee-voting window and tightening voter-list maintenance), which passed the Iowa Senate 30-18 on 2021-02-23.
Voted no on HF 2317 (replacing Iowa's graduated income tax with a 3.9% flat tax), which passed the Iowa Senate 32-16 on 2022-02-24.

researchNotes: Nunn's official issues page and Trone Garriott's campaign issues page present their priorities as category headings without expanded text in the fetched page content, so detail beyond the listed issue names was not available within the research budget. No 2025-2026 committee assignment listing was found for Nunn on Ballotpedia; only his 2023-2024 assignments are recorded here. Nunn's official-site press releases were searched for statements matching the guide's 15 issue categories; immigration enforcement and Israel aid were documented from his press releases, but abortion, guns, climate, taxes on high earners, tariffs, and the other issue statements were not directly and specifically addressed in the pages checked, so no positions were added for those. Biography gaps: Nunn's official biography does not give degree names, so degrees rely on Ballotpedia; Wikipedia lists a differently worded Cambridge degree (Master of Studies in international security).
